title: Write actions: preview, approval, and stale state
outcome: Bind approval to an exact operation and recheck it before an effect.
cue: Approve this operation, not this conversation.
version: Provider-neutral principles · Ruby 3.3 / Rails 7.2 lab · legacy Ruby 2.7 adaptation notes
useCase: Bind approval to an exact operation and recheck it before an effect.
benefits: A clear decision and a way to check it.
drawbacks: A conversation-level approved=true flag can authorize unrelated future actions. A model-generated idempotency key may change on every retry.

trace.title: Exact proposed action
trace.detail:
## Understand

A user approving “update this note” should not approve a later, different payload. Bind approval to an exact operation: actor, target, normalized arguments, relevant record version, scope, and expiry.

Make the preview readable in ordinary language.

At execution, reauthorize, compare the current record/version, check the approval identity, and apply a stable business idempotency key. If the operation changed or became stale, require a new preview.

The model cannot approve its own proposal.

Separate proposal, approval and execution status. A UI confirmation is not a database lock.

An approved write can still fail or have an unknown outcome. Keep an audit trail and reconciliation path.

The main course example remains read-only; the action sandbox illustrates these boundaries using synthetic in-memory data.

trace.title: Follow one input
trace.detail: Proposal → normalized preview → user approval → current authorization/version check → idempotent effect → recorded outcome. Test changed arguments, expired approval, a revoked actor, duplicate execution and acknowledgment loss.

trace.detail: A conversation-level approved=true flag can authorize unrelated future actions. A model-generated idempotency key may change on every retry.
